findings.title: Explicitly classify every malformed or unsupported successful open as cleanup-unconfirmed
findings.evidence: The draft requires cleanup-unconfirmed invalid_response for a valid original handle with nonnil upload, but then says malformed success maps to invalid_response without explicitly keeping the cleanup-unconfirmed discriminator. The plan separately names invalid handles and impossible uploads but does not remove this ambiguity. In existing Probe, settle with request=nil calls complete; complete can finish transport/release pins then call probe_finished, which refunds the probe hold. Unsupported success has no confirmed cleanup barrier, so mapping it as an ordinary invalid_response can enter that refund path. Current Session instead classifies every unsupported/malformed :ok result as {:cleanup_unconfirmed,:invalid_response}; malformed public success in ManagedH2Client likewise preserves negative cleanup evidence.
findings.required_change: State in both design and plan that every tuple tagged :ok that is not the exact valid HEAD {:ok, supported_original_handle, nil} result returns {:error, {:cleanup_unconfirmed, :invalid_response}, dropped}. This includes malformed arity, invalid/unsupported handle and every nonnil upload. Retain a supported original handle for cleanup when available; never retain arbitrary invalid handle/upload diagnostics. Actual Probe consumer must route this discriminator to hold/stop without probe_finished, including request=nil and transport_selection=nil. It must not fall through ordinary rejected/settle(request:nil)/complete. Existing raw cleanup-unconfirmed atom/tuple behavior retains the same rule. Add these variants to the already planned complete pure result cases and require direct source review of the consumer dispatch. Do not weaken existing assertions.
findings.verification_expected: Revised versioned documents and renewed design SPEC; later complete pure malformed-success cases and independent source review must show no ordinary refund on this discriminator. No runtime acceptance is inferred from this review.
